name: veterinary_clinic_system_015_run_maintenance_rebalance
instruction:
Run the end-of-month kennel capacity rebalance and deep-clean rotation as of the episode date. A run is eligible for 'maintenance' only if its current status is 'available' AND it has no reservation with status 'reserved' or 'checked_in' whose stay overlaps the episode date (check_in <= episode_date <= check_out). This must be derived from live data each episode; do not assume a fixed set of runs.

For each location, select the lowest-numbered eligible run (per-location string sort on run_number) and set its status to 'maintenance' with current_patient_id cleared. Additionally, the location that currently has the most occupied runs must also put its highest-numbered eligible run into maintenance, but only if that location has at least two eligible runs and the highest is different from the lowest. If the most-occupied location has zero or one eligible run, the extra selection is skipped. Do not pull a run from another location to satisfy the extra rule.

For every selected run, push an audit_log row with action='RUN_MAINTENANCE', actor='system', actor_role='housekeeping', target_collection='boarding_runs', target_id=<run_id>, details='Deep-clean <run_number> at <location_name> assigned by batch <batch_code>', occurred_at=<episode_date with time>.

Create exactly one ops_reports row 'maintenance_rebalance' keyed by the live batch_code, with: episode_date, total_maintenance (int), by_location (dict {location_name: count}), selected_runs (list of {run_id, run_number, location_name, run_type, board_night_price, reason}), and lost_nights_7 = total_maintenance * 7. The board_night_price must come from the BOARD-NIGHT line item of that run's location fee_schedule. Overwrite any existing 'maintenance_rebalance' row for this batch. Do not modify reservations, daily logs, or any run that is not selected.
_max_steps_note: Measured against a live container in the QC session; placeholder because this codegen-only session cannot run gold.
_par_steps_note: Measured against a live container in the QC session; placeholder because this codegen-only session cannot run gold.

success_criteria.summary: Recompute eligible runs from live data and episode date. The set of runs with status='maintenance' must equal the selected set. Every selected run has current_patient_id cleared and all other fields unchanged; every non-selected run is byte-identical to seed. Exactly one audit_log entry per selected run with the exact action/actor/details and no extra audit_log entries for this batch. Exactly one ops_reports 'maintenance_rebalance' row for this batch with correct total, by_location, selected_runs, and lost_nights_7. Aggregate counts are recomputed two independent ways (raw-row Python filter and SQL GROUP BY/COUNT) and must agree. All collections outside the blast radius are byte-identical to seed.

checks.expect: Exactly the computed selected runs are status='maintenance' with current_patient_id cleared; all others unchanged
One RUN_MAINTENANCE entry per selected run, no extras
Exactly one maintenance_rebalance row per batch with live counts and list
Every aggregate total and by-location count for selected runs agrees between raw-row Python derivation and independent SQL GROUP BY/COUNT

hazards: Reservation-locked runs: at the default episode date 2026-09-30, the snapshot shows runs K06 (reserved 65 from 2026-09-23 and reserved 6 from 2026-09-24), K07 (reserved 7 from 2026-09-12 to 2026-09-30), C10 (reserved 17 from 2026-09-23 and reserved 85 from 2026-09-20), X15 (reserved 128 from 2026-09-28), and X17 (reserved 74 from 2026-09-27) have overlapping reserved/checked_in stays and must NOT be set to maintenance. A solution that flips every 'available' run to maintenance hits these and fails the canary.

Boundary precision: the check_out on reservation 7 is exactly 2026-09-30 (the default episode date). Using a strict 'check_out < episode_date' overlap test would wrongly make K07 eligible; the interval overlap must be inclusive on both endpoints (check_in <= episode_date <= check_out). The episode date jitters ±3 days in env.py, so the set of ineligible runs shifts every episode.

Run-number sorting is per-location and string-based: the run_number prefixes are K, C, and X, so a naive global string sort would pick C09/C10 before any K run. The mission requires the lowest- and highest-numbered eligible run within each location_id.

The 'extra' run is tied to the location with the most occupied runs, which in this seed is location 1 (runs K01-K05 occupied). A red-herring solution that picks the location with large_dog runs (location 3) and sets X17 or X15 fails; X17/X15 are also ineligible due to overlapping reservations.

Idempotency on re-run: the ops_reports row must be overwritten by batch_code, audit_log entries must not be duplicated, and a second run must leave the same set of runs in 'maintenance' with the same state.

uniqueness_report.differentiation_note: Redesigned around the live 10x seed snapshot: the old v1 rule of a fixed 3-4 run change no longer holds. The v2 mission requires the agent to derive eligibility from live reservation overlaps, to handle the fact that location 1 is the only occupied location, to avoid large_dog-type red herrings, and to produce an auditable report with dual-path aggregate verification.
